annotation_description: Sleight of Hand vs Opt on turn 1 is a classic sequencing question. Opt's scry 1 then draw lets you see one card and either keep or bottom it, then draw the next. Sleight of Hand looks at two cards and picks one. Generally Sleight of Hand digs slightly deeper (sees 2 cards vs Opt's effective 2 cards but with different selection). However, Opt is an instant and could be saved for the opponent's end step to keep mana open for responses. On turn 1 with only 1 mana available and no interactive spells that cost U in hand (Three Steps Ahead costs more), there's no meaningful advantage to holding up mana. The choice between these two cantrips is extremely close and largely preference-dependent. Sleight of Hand is a reasonable choice here since there's nothing to hold up mana for.

message: Discard a creature card instead of discarding two cards?
annotation_description: Discarded Multiversal Passage, their only land in hand, when they have 5 lands on board and need to reach 9 mana to cast Sunderflock (no Elementals in play to reduce cost). Every land drop matters for reaching their win condition.

message: Select card to discard (selected 1 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: With Winternight Stories' discard clause ('discard two cards unless you discard a creature card'), Sonnet Teach chose to discard Spider-Sense (non-creature) as the first card, forcing them to discard a second card as well. They have two Eddymurk Crabs in hand, so discarding one creature card would have satisfied the condition with only one discard, saving an entire card.

Gem25P Stoic declined to activate Fountainport's abilities during their main phase when they had 8 lands available and nothing else to do with their mana. They could have used Fountainport to create a Fish token ({3}, {T}, Pay 1 life) to start building a board presence, or created a Treasure token ({4}, {T}) for future mana flexibility. With an Eddymurk Crab threatening them and no creatures of their own, generating any board presence or resources would be valuable. The reasoning mentions 'no castable spells' but overlooks that Fountainport's activated abilities are available and Stock Up (3 mana) is in hand and castable.

Casting Get Lost during their own combat phase rather than waiting until the opponent's upkeep/draw step or end of opponent's turn. This unnecessarily uses mana now, leaving less mana available for counterspells during the opponent's turn, and gives away information about hand contents.

message: Discard a creature card instead of discarding two cards?
annotation_description: Discarded Eddymurk Crab which costs only {U}{U} with 12 instants/sorceries in graveyard, keeping Sunderflock which costs {9} without any Elemental in play to reduce its cost. The Eddymurk Crab was immediately castable as a 5/5 flash threat, while Sunderflock is essentially a dead card without an Elemental on board. Furthermore, Eddymurk Crab on the battlefield would have reduced Sunderflock's cost to {2}{U}{U}, making the sequencing even worse.

With 2 untapped Steam Vents (producing RR or UR), Sonnet Teach passed with nothing and then had to discard 2 cards from a 9-card hand. They had 3 Burst Lightnings in hand - casting 2 at the opponent's face would deal 4 damage, reduce hand to exactly 7 (no discard needed), and add instants to graveyard (reducing Eddymurk Crab/Sunderflock costs). Instead they wasted 2 mana and lost 2 cards to discard.

Gem25P Stoic declined to activate Restless Anchorage to attack when the opponent was completely tapped out. With Sunken Citadel (producing 2W for land abilities) and Floodfarm Verge available, they could animate Restless Anchorage (1WU) and attack for 2 flying damage plus create a Map token, with zero risk since the opponent has all lands tapped.

In a control mirror, Restless Anchorage is a premium win condition that can attack through counter-heavy boards. Playing Sunken Citadel instead means delaying the deployment of a key threat. The Sunken Citadel's double-mana for land abilities (Fountainport) is a marginal advantage compared to having a creature-land that can pressure the opponent's life total.

message: Discard a creature card instead of discarding two cards?
annotation_description: Discarded the last Eddymurk Crab when it would cost only {U}{U} to cast (7 instants/sorceries in graveyard reducing its cost by 7). With Eddymurk Crab on the battlefield (MV 7), Sunderflock would also cost only {U}{U}. This Crab+Sunderflock line is the deck's primary win condition. By discarding all 4 Eddymurk Crabs, Sunderflock now costs a full 9 mana with no discount enabler.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 4, min 4)
annotation_description: Discarding Abandon Attachments (which can turn any dead card into 2 fresh cards for just 2 mana) over a third copy of Spell Snare (a narrow counter that only hits exactly 2-mana spells). Already keeping one Spell Snare plus Spell Pierce for countermagic coverage.

Opponent is at 2 life. Gem25P Stoic has Restless Anchorage available to activate ({1}{W}{U} to become a 2/3 flyer) and could attack for lethal damage. Instead, they passed without activating it or taking any action during combat, missing a likely lethal attack.

With the opponent at 2 life, Gem25P Stoic should have played Restless Anchorage from hand. While it enters tapped, it would be available next turn to animate into a 2/3 flyer and attack for lethal against the 2-life opponent. Missing this land drop delays the clock by a full turn.

Opponent is at 2 life. Gem25P Stoic has Restless Anchorage on the battlefield and 8 lands available. Activating Restless Anchorage for {1}{W}{U} would create a 2/3 flyer. However, the player chose to pass without doing anything this main phase. While they mention activating it during opponent's end step, that doesn't help - they need to attack with it, which means they need to activate it on their own turn (ideally before combat). Since this is postcombat main, the attack window has already passed this turn. The real mistake was likely not activating Restless Anchorage before combat to attack for lethal with the 2/3 flyer. Passing here without casting anything meaningful (like Elspeth who could also create tokens) wastes a turn when the opponent is at 2 life.

At 2 life with 7 lands (only one tapped), Sonnet Teach has Winternight Stories in graveyard available to Harmonize. With creatures in the graveyard (Eddymurk Crab x4, Sunderflock x2), tapping a creature could reduce the Harmonize cost. However, there are no creatures on board to tap. The Harmonize cost is {4}{U} = 5 mana, and with 7 lands (6 untapped), this is castable. Drawing 3 cards and discarding a creature could help find more answers. That said, the player has a reasonable hand with multiple counterspells (2x Spell Snare, Spell Pierce) and interaction (Into the Flood Maw, Burst Lightning), so holding up countermagic at 2 life is also defensible. The decision to pass without casting anything is reasonable given the need to hold up counters at such low life.

Failed to play Island from hand before casting Sunderflock. At 2 life, maximizing available mana is critical for holding up protection spells. Playing the land first is strictly better sequencing - it provides an additional mana source for subsequent turns and potentially allows holding up more interaction after casting the threat.

Gem25P Stoic passed their entire postcombat main phase with 8 untapped lands, doing nothing while the opponent sits at 2 life with all lands tapped and no board. They even had to discard to hand size, wasting cards. The reasoning incorrectly states 'the game should be over' when the opponent is still alive at 2 life.
